e.etymology: A Spanish-language form of Oziel, an older Bible spelling of Uzziel, Hebrew for God is my strength. It is used mainly in Mexico and among Mexican American families.
A modern spelling with two readings: for boys it follows Josiah and the Biblical name Asaiah, and for girls it is a variant of Asia or of the Arabic name Asiya.
A respelling of Alani, the Hawaiian word for the orange and the orange tree. Many parents choose it for its closeness to lani, Hawaiian for sky or heaven, as in Leilani.

assoc.t: Alani Nu energy drinks (spelled Alani)

e.meaning: blend of Anna, grace, and Liese, from Elisabeth
e.etymology: A German compound of Anna and Liese, a short form of Elisabeth. Anna is from Hebrew for grace, and Elisabeth from Hebrew for my God is an oath.

assoc.t: Princess Anneliese in Barbie as the Princess and the Pauper

e.etymology: From Old Irish cían, long-lasting or ancient. In Irish legend Cian is the father of the god Lugh, and a later Cian was a son-in-law of the high king Brian Boru.
e.note: Outside Ireland it is often misread as SEE-an or SIGH-an; the Irish sound is KEE-un.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage with no older meaning, shaped by Isla, Lyla and Nylah with the fashionable Z opening.
In the US it is given mainly to boys in Spanish-speaking families; Eider and Eyder are men's names in Colombia. In Basque, Eider is a girls' name from eder, beautiful.

assoc.t: eider, a sea duck whose down fills eiderdown quilts

e.etymology: From Greek Magdalene, woman from Magdala, the byname of Mary Magdalene in the Gospels. Magdala was a village on the Sea of Galilee whose name comes from Hebrew migdal, tower.

assoc.t: Mary Magdalene, follower of Jesus in the Gospels
Magdalene laundries, harsh Irish church-run institutions

e.etymology: A modern Indian name ending in ansh, from Sanskrit amsha, a part or portion. Name lists gloss it as ray of light or a part of Lord Vishnu, but the first element has no settled Sanskrit source.
An American form of the Danish and Norwegian surname Iversen, son of Iver, from the Old Norse name Ívarr. As a first name it follows Anderson and Jackson.

assoc.t: Allen Iverson, Hall of Fame NBA guard

e.meaning: from the Swiss city, whose Celtic name refers to a river bend
e.etymology: Taken from the Swiss city, Latin Genava, probably a Celtic name for a bending river or estuary. As a girls' name it has also been confused with Genevieve and Ginevra.

assoc.t: Geneva, Swiss city of diplomacy and watchmaking
Geneva Conventions, treaties on conduct in war

e.etymology: A medieval German short form of Johannes, the Latin form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. It spread across Scandinavia and the Low Countries from the 14th century.
namesakes: Hans Christian Andersen (Danish author of fairy tales)
Hans Gruber (Alan Rickman's villain in Die Hard)

assoc.t: Prince Hans, the villain of Disney's Frozen

e.meaning: little Marcus, a Roman name tied to the god Mars
e.etymology: The Spanish, Portuguese, Czech and Polish form of Marcella, feminine of Marcellus, a Roman family name formed as a diminutive of Marcus.
The English word wisdom, from Old English wis, wise, and the ending -dom. It is a virtue name in the line of Faith and Justice, and it is well established in Nigeria and Ghana.
An English surname for someone who lived in a dale, from Old English dael, valley. It became a first name in the 19th century and was at its height in the US in the 1950s.
namesakes: Dale Carnegie (author of How to Win Friends and Influence People)
Dale Evans (singing cowgirl and wife of Roy Rogers)

assoc.t: Dale, of Disney's chipmunk duo Chip 'n' Dale
Dale Earnhardt, NASCAR legend, and his son Dale Jr.
dale, an old English word for a valley

e.meaning: form of Anthony, from the Roman family name Antonius
e.etymology: The German, Scandinavian and Slavic form of Anthony, from Antonius, a Roman family name of unknown meaning. English borrowed it from German and other northern European languages.
namesakes: Anton Yelchin (actor who played Chekov in Star Trek)
Anton Ego (the food critic in Ratatouille)

e.etymology: A modern American coinage, close to Amari and to the stage name of R&B singer Omarion, whose rise with the group B2K in the early 2000s matches the name's peak.
An English surname for someone who lived among rushes, the waterside plants, and an anglicized Irish surname. As a first name it also reads as the English word for speed and hurry.

assoc.t: rush, the English word for hurry or a thrill
Rush Limbaugh, conservative talk radio host
Rush, the Canadian rock trio

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that reworks Xavier, by way of Zavier, with the -ian ending of Davian and Julian.
An English surname from the many places called Milton, from Old English mylen, mill, or middel, middle, and tun, settlement. It is also used as a first name in Latin America.
namesakes: Milton Hershey (founder of the Hershey chocolate company)

assoc.t: John Milton, poet of Paradise Lost
Hurricane Milton, which struck Florida in October 2024
Milton, the stapler-guarding worker in Office Space

e.etymology: An English surname from the Norman personal name Warnier, the same name as German Werner, built from Germanic words for guard and army. Some families got it from warrener, a keeper of rabbit warrens.

assoc.t: Warner Bros., Hollywood film and television studio
Warner Music Group, major record company
Warner, Elle's ex-boyfriend in Legally Blonde

e.etymology: A modern American coinage joining the Ja- opening of Jada and Jaliyah with the sound of Alayah and Malaya.
An English occupational surname from Middle English kervere, a wood-cutter or sculptor. In the US it carries the memory of scientist George Washington Carver.

assoc.t: George Washington Carver, agricultural scientist
Raymond Carver, short story writer

e.etymology: The name of the Greek god of love, from Greek eros, desire. His Roman counterpart is Cupid. As a given name it is used in Italy and Latin America.

assoc.t: Eros, the Greek god of love, the Roman Cupid
Eros, Versace men's cologne

e.note: Eros is the root of the word erotic and is used in English for sexual love, so the name carries that overtone.

e.etymology: In Jewish use a spelling of Hebrew Liora, my light. The name was also common in the US around 1900, when it may have been a contraction of Leonora.
A medieval spelling of Ralph that shows how the name was once said. Ralph is from Old Norse Rathulfr, counsel and wolf. Rafe is also a short form of Raphael and Rafael.
namesakes: Rafe Cameron (antagonist of Netflix's Outer Banks)

e.meaning: something handed down, a lasting inheritance
e.etymology: A respelling of the English word legacy, from Medieval Latin legatia, the office of a deputy, later a bequest. It is a modern word name in the style of Journey and Destiny.

assoc.t: Subaru Legacy sedan (spelled Legacy)

e.etymology: The English verb adore, from Latin adorare, to worship. Related forms such as Adora and the French Adorée have a longer history as names.
A respelling of Chosen, the past participle of choose, which became a given name in the 2020s. As a name it echoes the Biblical idea of being chosen by God.

assoc.t: The Chosen, TV drama about the life of Jesus

e.etymology: The everyday short form of Nicholas, from Greek Nikolaos, built from nike, victory, and laos, people.
namesakes: Nick Jonas (singer in the Jonas Brothers)
Nick Saban (college football coach with seven national titles)
Nick Carraway (narrator of The Great Gatsby)

assoc.t: Nick, short for the Nickelodeon children's TV network
Saint Nick, a nickname for Santa Claus
nick, a small cut; British slang for steal or jail

e.etymology: From Sanskrit ravi, the sun, one of the names of the Hindu sun god Surya. It is used across India; the Bengali form is Robi or Rabi.
namesakes: Ravi Shankar (sitar master who taught George Harrison)
Ravi Ross (character on Disney Channel's Jessie and Bunk'd)

e.etymology: A Swedish name of unknown origin, first recorded in 1597 for a German immigrant to Sweden. It is sometimes glossed as calm and often linked with Latin stella, star, but neither is proven.
namesakes: Stellan Skarsgård (Swedish actor in Mamma Mia!, Dune and Andor)
